note: Standing verdicts on elaboration-level substitutions. `scripts/check_elaboration_drift.py --classify` matches the silent set of a migration against these and reports only what is left over, so a toolchain bump costs a reading of the classes upstream introduced rather than a reading of every declaration they touched. A class is only recorded here once its anchor -- a fact that decides the meaning and that can be stated in terms existing at both toolchains -- compiles on both trees. Anchors live in docs/provenance/elaboration-adjudication-*.lean.
how_a_class_is_checked: `removes` and `adds` are the machine-checkable content of the verdict; `key` only names it and `change` only reads it aloud. A class fires on a declaration when every constant in `removes` left that statement. A declaration is classified only when the classes that fired between them account for BOTH sides: every constant that left is in some fired class's `removes`, and every constant that arrived is in some fired class's `adds`. Matching on the departure alone would certify `setOf -> anything`, and would swallow an unrelated substitution riding along in the same statement. `adds` is a superset rather than an equality because a constant the substitution introduces may already occur in the statement for other reasons, in which case it is not a new arrival; that direction is safe, since it can only leave an arrival unaccounted for and so fail closed.
